edits.headline: Lula wins a fourth term as president of Brazil
edits.subheadline: World leaders congratulated Lula on his election win and Bolsonaro refused to concede, The Guardian reported.
editorialBody: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term in Brazil's presidential runoff, NPR reported. World leaders congratulated him and Bolsonaro refused to concede, The Guardian reported.
Brent crude fell below $110 a barrel on hopes of a deal with Iran, and Brazilian stocks fell, CoinDesk reported.
In Serbia, people celebrated after Vučić, the veteran ruler, lost an election to a student-led protest movement, BBC News reported.
Meta plans a $95bn stock offering to pay for its AI expansion, the Financial Times reported. Verizon's shares rose after a rise in subscribers impressed Wall Street, MarketWatch reported.

In the US, redistricting is not going as Republicans hoped, NPR reported. A Wichita State University student was charged with rape, the second such case on the campus this month, the New York Post reported.

Shares in Borr Drilling fell 11% after five people went missing from a rig that sank off Gabon, Bloomberg reported. Jordan arrested three suspects over a church attack in a dawn raid, Al Jazeera reported.
Taiwan's tea growers are letting nature take back their land as climate pressures grow, Mongabay reported.
